explanation: Android layers product-facing application and framework behavior above Linux. Binder IPC connects applications, system services and vendor services. HAL contracts isolate framework capabilities from hardware-specific implementation, while AIDL defines typed process boundaries. Synchronous IPC, service lifecycle and thread pools are architectural concerns because a slow or cyclic service dependency can freeze unrelated product behavior.

Android Automotive OS adds vehicle-oriented framework services and the Vehicle HAL. A vehicle property is not simply a network signal: it has identifiers, areas, access modes, change behavior, permissions and availability semantics. The VHAL adapts vehicle-specific interfaces, car services implement platform policy, and applications consume stable APIs. Safety or final actuator authority normally remains in vehicle controllers, not in an HMI application.

Platform customization should use supported APIs, overlays, configuration and bounded vendor services. Deep framework forks increase migration, security and compatibility cost. Common-feature architecture should provide a stable capability model and product-owned presentation without duplicating core services.
whyItMatters: AAOS features cross application, framework, vendor and vehicle-controller boundaries.
Clean platform contracts allow several products to share services while preserving vehicle-specific capability and authority.
activities: Trace feature call and data paths
Allocate policy, adaptation and actuator authority
Design lifecycle, restart and unavailable-data behavior
Test permissions, SELinux, load and compatibility
automotiveExample: A climate application calls a car-service API. The service validates user state and policy, then sends a bounded request through the VHAL adaptation to a body controller. The body controller enforces actuator limits and reports actual state. Product variants declare supported zones rather than forking the service.
commonMistakes: Mapping raw CAN signals directly into application contracts
Holding locks across synchronous Binder calls
Placing vehicle safety policy in the UI application
Customizing core framework without migration ownership
Showing stale vehicle data without availability semantics
